text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @oncall-maya — Dedicated pool 'eu-west-1-reserved' reporting sustained saturation. Autoscaler hit max_nodes, request queue for reserved tenants growing. Affected tenant: AcmeCorp-Ent (reserved contract). Current queued requests: 37, 95th p99 latency spike to 14s, 429 throttle rate up 11% in last 5m. Please ack and triage.

oncall-maya: acked. I'm looking now, pulling metrics. Can someone paste the autoscaler status and recent scale events?

sara-eng: grabbing metrics — showing rapid queue growth after a noisy tenant ramp at ~1808002000. Autoscaler config for eu-west-1-reserved: min_nodes=8, max_nodes=20, scale_step=2, cooldown=120s. Looks like we hit max_nodes=20 at 1808002103.

raj-ops: logs from router showing fallback attempts: `route->dedicated-pool-eu-burst` failing because routing policy pins reserved tenant to reserved pool. We'll need to relax pinning or create temporary exception.

eli-support: customer success reported increased 429s for AcmeCorp-Ent - trying to correlate. Ticket #CS-4721 shows spike starting ~10:12 UTC. Customer-facing impact: degraded throughput, some requests queued >20s.

oncall-maya: quick plan: 1) preempt best-effort workloads in reserved pool (low-risk) 2) bump autoscaler max_nodes from 20->30 as temporary emergency 3) open fallback routing for AcmeCorp to eu-burst for non-latency-critical routes 4) engage infra to add capacity. I'll start with 1 and 2.

sara-eng: +1. Preemption call: `POST /admin/pools/eu-west-1-reserved/preempt` (dry-run=false) will evict non-reserved jobs.

oncall-maya: running preempt now: ```
$ curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADM" \
  https://controlplane.internal/admin/pools/eu-west-1-reserved/preempt \
  -d '{"evict_priority":"best_effort"}'
{"status":"started","evicted_count":12}
```

oncall-maya: evicted 12 best-effort workloads, freed ~3 GPUs. Queue dropped from 37 -> 29 in the first minute.

matt-infra: I see the autoscaler at max_nodes=20. I can bump the limit but need oncall to authorize emergency change to avoid violating billing/reservation constraints. ETA to provision additional machines if we increase limit: ~35-50 minutes for new nodes, but we can unpin and route immediately.

oncall-maya: bumping autoscaler max to 30 for emergency. Command: `PATCH /admin/autoscalers/eu-west-1-reserved` with `max_nodes=30`.

oncall-maya: ```
$ http patch https://controlplane.internal/admin/autoscalers/eu-west-1-reserved \
  Authorization:"Bearer $ADM" max_nodes=30
{"result":"ok","old_max":20,"new_max":30}
```

sara-eng: autoscaler accepted new max. But note scale-up depends on node pool capacity; if cloud quota prevents immediate nodes we still rely on fallback routing.

oncall-maya: enabling temporary routing exception for AcmeCorp-Ent (non-critical endpoints) to move to `dedicated-pool-eu-burst`. Command: `POST /routing/overrides` -> creating rule.

oncall-maya: rule created. Routing shows ~8 connections started flowing to eu-burst, queue for reserved pool down to 14.

eli-support: reporting back to customer: sent note — "We've activated mitigation steps; some requests are routed to a burst pool; we expect normalized performance in 10-20 minutes, engineering investigating root cause." Customer responded: "App still slow but improved vs 10 minutes ago".

raj-ops: investigating noisy tenant — tenant id `nv-49` shows a sudden increase in concurrent sessions from their internal batch job. They are not on reserved capacity. Looks like they leaked into the reserved pool via misconfigured placement override. I'm pausing their jobs now.

raj-ops: paused nv-49 batch jobs (policy enforcement). Freed 4 GPUs. Queue now 7. Throttle rate down to ~2%.

oncall-maya: good. I'm going to hand this to @sara-eng for monitoring shift while I start a deeper postmortem. Handoff notes: actions taken = preempted 12 best-effort jobs, bumped autoscaler max 20->30, created routing override for AcmeCorp-Ent, paused noisy tenant nv-49. Current state: queue=7, p99 latency 2.3s, 429 rate 1.1%. Please monitor for 30m and escalate to infra if nodes don't come up.

sara-eng: taking over monitoring. I'll keep this thread updated. Next steps I'm scheduling: 1) confirm new nodes coming up with matt-infra 2) revert routing override once stable 3) run quick audit for placement overrides to prevent recurrence.

matt-infra: FYI — provisioning in progress, requested 6 additional GPUs into `eu-west-1-reserved`. Cloud quota check passed, expected ready at ~1808002860 (~6.5 minutes).

sara-eng: noted. I'll wait for node arrival. Meanwhile I set an alert for queue>10 and 429s>3% to page.

customer-success: updated AcmeCorp contact with ETA and mitigation details. They asked if we can guarantee no data cross-over — confirmed all routed traffic to burst pool still respects tenant isolation and KMS. They asked for post-incident follow-up.

eli-support: logging incident in support tracker with severity=P1 for customer SLA; linking engineering thread. Ticket updated.

oncall-maya: thanks team — handing off fully to @sara-eng. I'll join postmortem and help with remediation plan. :thumbsup:

sara-eng: taking it from here. Current metrics: queue=3, p99=1.8s, 429=0.8%. Monitoring. If stable for 30m we'll close this page and open a follow-up for root cause analysis (placement override + autoscaler hard limit).

incident-bot: note — paging window closed for @oncall-maya. Monitoring alerts remain active.

matt-infra: new nodes are healthy and joined the pool at 1808002805; capacity increased by 6 GPUs. Autoscaler now scaling to 26 nodes.

sara-eng: confirmed. Rolling back routing override after confirming no regression. Revert command run. Queue now fully drained.

eli-support: closing customer-facing update: sent final note and proposed postmortem summary and timeline.

raj-ops: I kicked off a config lint job across placement policies to find accidental pin overrides. Found 2 recent PRs that relaxed placement rules — filing change request to enforce reserved-only placements.

oncall-maya: noted for postmortem. Thanks everyone. I'll craft action items: 1) increase autoscaler safety margin or implement emergency burst lane for reserved tenants 2) add guardrails in PR review for placement rules 3) add a runbook step to allow temporary routing exceptions.

sara-eng: copying actions into incident board and assigning owners. Monitoring will stay on this for 30m then we'll decide close.

customer-success: customer acknowledged final update and will wait for postmortem. Marking as notified.

incident-bot: thread activity paused. Last state: stable.
